summary: Transient pin reset for subset of sessions during header-based token migration causes mixed-model responses and fallbacks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Notos Analytics) reported a spike of mixed-model outputs and 5xxs for a subset of users immediately after their SSO provider rolled out a header-based session token rename (X-SSO-Session -> X-SSO-Auth). During a staged canary (15% traffic), approximately 8% of the affected tenant's requests lost model-version pin affinity and were routed to the degraded variant, causing both quality regressions and increased cost due to fallback retries.

Impact:
- ~8% of tenant sessions receiving mixed responses (legacy variant + new canary) for ~45 minutes.
- Rate of 5xx increased from 0.2% -> 1.4% for that tenant's route.
- Customer-facing feature regressions (context continuity loss) for a subset of end-users.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1), Redwood hosted API, tenant on enterprise plan with model pin set in route config.
- Canary weight: 15% for rw-gpt-35-quantized-v2.
- Edge proxy (ingress) was in the middle of an auth header normalization rollout.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Customer rotated SSO provider header name at edge (X-SSO-Session -> X-SSO-Auth) in canary slice.
2. Requests from the rotated cohort arrived with mixed headers while orchestrator epoch updates were in-flight.
3. Orchestrator's pin reconciliation path matched on token header value; missing header treated as new session and triggered a pin refresh flow.
4. Some sessions lost previous model-version affinity and were sent to fallback policy (degraded variant) while cache warms.

Observed behavior:
- Partial pin eviction for subset of sessions coincident with header rotation window.
- Orchestrator logs show pin-evict events with reason "auth-token-mismatch" and subsequent dispatches to fallback variant.
- Edge logs show header key present in 92% of requests and absent/malformed in remaining 8% during the window.
- Canary metric (model-selection-consistency) dropped for the tenant.

Expected behavior:
- Header rename should be handled by auth normalization without triggering pin eviction.
- Pin reconciliation should detect token migration semantics and preserve pin when equivalent session identity can be derived.

Logs / Evidence:
- Sample request IDs: rq_3f9a2bcd, rq_3f9a2bd0, rq_3f9a2c01
- Orchestrator trace: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/8f4a... (redacted) shows pin eviction calls and fallback routing.
- Edge access logs: s3://redwood-logs/notos/2025-03-18/edge-rotate.log
- Metrics snapshots attached to ticket (model-selection-consistency, 5xx-rate, fallback-rate).

Temporary workaround applied by Support:
- Rolled back the canary auth header rewrite at edge for Notos slice at 2025-03-18T21:12:00Z which stopped new pin evictions.
- Forced a targeted route refresh to rebind affected sessions to pinned model (manual reconciliation command executed by SRE).

Root-cause hypothesis (current):
- The orchestrator's pin reconciliation assumes session identity derives solely from a single header key. During header rollout, missing header was treated as session change rather than a migration, causing an eviction path that lacks a migration mapping.
- Timing window between edge normalization and orchestrator epoch update created a race where some requests had pre-migration tokens and others had post-migration tokens.

Next steps / Action items:
1. Engineering to add migration-aware pin reconciliation: treat header rename/aliasing as identity-preserving when configured mapping exists (ENG-2197).
2. Add guard in orchestrator to delay pin eviction by a small hysteresis window if auth header transitions are detected for a cohort.
3. Update canary runbook to include header-migration checklist and to pin traffic to avoid partial eviction (Confluence updated).
4. SRE to run a reconciliation job to verify no residual split pins exist for Notos tenant and to generate a one-off audit of pin stability across affected routes.

Customer communications:
- Notified customer of rollback and mitigation at 21:25 UTC; committed to timeline for a permanent fix (ETA 5 business days).
- Customer requested post-incident verification and export of affected request IDs for their audit.

Resolution (current):
- Mitigation applied (edge rollback + manual reconciliation). Issue is under engineering investigation for a permanent fix.

2025-03-18 21:10 UTC - SRE (A. Chen): Confirmed edge rewrite in canary. Observed ~8% requests missing expected header key. Rolled back the rewrite for Notos canary slice at 21:12 UTC; fallback rate started to decline.

2025-03-18 22:05 UTC - Luca Morales (Orchestrator Eng): Found pin-evict trace with reason 'auth-token-mismatch'. Hypothesis: missing header treated as new identity. Creating ENG task to implement migration aliasing and hysteresis (ENG-2197).
2025-03-19 09:00 UTC - Priya Shah (Support): Customer acknowledged mitigation but requested export of affected request IDs (provided S3 link). Scheduling follow-up call for 2025-03-20.

2025-03-19 14:30 UTC - Engineering (Luca Morales): Draft design posted at https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/issues/2197. Will aim for patch in the next sprint; planning a hotfix if risk warrants it.
investigation_notes: Checked orchestrator's pin reconciliation timeline. Confirmed race window correlates with edge canary rewrite rollout timestamp. Verified that pin eviction code path does not consult session aliasing table. Edge normalization should have provided backward-compatible alias header but migration was partial at canary. SRE successfully forced reconciliation on affected tenant routes and observed pin rebind in subsequent requests.
workaround: Rolled back edge header rewrite for the tenant canary slice; executed targeted route refresh to rebind pins; customer advised to pause header rename until orchestration fix is deployed.
resolution: Mitigation in place; engineering task ENG-2197 created for a permanent fix (migration-aware pin reconciliation and hysteresis). Pending code change and release verification.
follow_up: Post-mortem to be scheduled after ENG-2197 lands. Update canary migration runbook and add automated verification checks for header-based identity changes.
